examples.trans: I am going against all my principles.

examples.text: Вообще гольф — это лучшее, во что я играл в свою жизнь!
examples.trans: In general, golf is the best thing I have played in my life!

meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'нцип'). Common masculine noun meaning 'principles' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Иду против всех своих принципов.
examples.trans: I am going against all my principles.

examples.text: Сейчас деньги важнее любых глупых принципов.
examples.trans: Now money is more important than any silly principles.

examples.text: В принципе, вкус нормальный и не плохой.
examples.trans: In principle, the taste is fine and not bad.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'everything', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Всё, договорились, твоё условие принято.
examples.trans: That is it, we agreed, your condition is accepted.

examples.text: Всё, мы с тобой договорились.
examples.trans: That is it, you and I have a deal.

examples.text: Будешь курьером по доставке еды, всё, разговор окончен.
examples.trans: You will be a food delivery courier, that is all, the conversation is over.

meanings.en: to agree, to come to an arrangement
meanings.note: Prefix 'до-' marks reaching a boundary or finishing the remainder of an action (stem 'говориться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'agreed', paired with 'договариваться'.

examples.text: Договоримся на завтра.
examples.trans: We'll arrange something for tomorrow.

examples.text: Мы договорились.
examples.trans: We've agreed.

examples.text: Позвони мне вечером. Договоримся на завтра.
examples.trans: Call me this evening. We'll arrange something for tomorrow.

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'словие'). Common neuter noun meaning 'condition' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Всё, договорились, твоё условие принято.
examples.trans: That is it, we agreed, your condition is accepted.

examples.text: Посмотрите, какие тут условия.
examples.trans: Look what the conditions are like here.

examples.text: У меня есть одно условие.
examples.trans: I have one condition.

meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'нятый'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('accepted / deal').

examples.text: Всё, договорились, твоё условие принято.
examples.trans: That is it, we agreed, your condition is accepted.

examples.text: Нет, мы можем принять их или пытаться остаться в прошлом.
examples.trans: No, we can accept them or try to stay in the past.

meanings.note: Prefix 'во-' ('into, up') marks inward or upward movement (stem 'звращаться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'are returning', paired with 'вернуться'.

examples.text: Он всегда поздно возвращается домой.
examples.trans: He always comes home late.

examples.text: Зло всегда возвращается.
examples.trans: Evil always comes back.

examples.text: Запомните: зло всегда возвращается к правителю.
examples.trans: Remember: evil always comes back to the ruler.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'on, onto', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Я надеюсь, что у нас есть целая жизнь.
examples.trans: I hope that we have a whole life.

examples.text: Наш шеф уволил курьера по доставке еды.
examples.trans: Our chef fired the food delivery courier.

examples.text: У нас есть целая жизнь.
examples.trans: We have a whole life.

meanings.note: Entered Russian via Polish 'kuchnia' and Middle High German 'küchen', ultimately from Late Latin 'coquina' (from 'coquere', to cook).

examples.text: Максим, иди лучше на кухню работай.
examples.trans: Maxim, go work in the kitchen instead.

examples.text: Потому что я его с кухни выгнал.
examples.trans: Because I kicked him out of the kitchen.

examples.text: Макс, ты сегодня возвращаешься на кухню.
examples.trans: Max, today you are returning to the kitchen.
